assembly_sequence: Identify FRONT on the base. Motor-contact face is the broad flat side; motor head/washer pockets face down in the assembled rover.
Insert the six M3 rail nuts into the underside hex pockets. Bolt the two identical rails to the top: one is rotated180degrees. End stops face inward; the clear bay is73.025×149.225.
Thread both12mm powerbank straps through the four base slots. Fit the centered low bank, leaving the required charging and output ports accessible through the open ends. Close straps gently.

Fit all four existing motor/block/shaft/wheel groups to their matching holes. Preserve the stock group geometry. Front and rear hole positions differ; do not substitute a mirrored front pair for the rear.
Fit the line tracker below the base with the supplied3mm spacers or the existing stock spacer hardware appropriate to the actual sensor height.
Fit six40.5mm deck posts at X±48,Y−88,0,+88. Use the sixM3×50 support screws, bottom washers, top washers and nuts. Tighten evenly without crushing PLA.
Before closing the upper deck, route wires clear of wheels and shafts. Fit the motor battery on the rear upper deck; set the slot to its actual mounting-hole pitch between65and90mm.
Install the Pi and UNO on their6mm detachable standoffs. Refit the complete original front head to the source opening and hole pattern.

With power off and the rover lifted, turn each wheel through a full revolution and verify plugs, wires and screw ends clear the moving parts. The exact local motor fit is preserved; the full new assembly still requires this check.
